doc.title: Quincy Jones — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: On being an NEA Jazz Master, 'no boxes', Stanley Crouch and Wynton
summary: Jones values the recognition but says some quarters have boxed him in. He says he is not ashamed of Thriller, that if you can do all of it you should, and that he does not care what Stanley Crouch thinks.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: I love – listen. I’ve always loved what that’s about, is having that recognition of one of our most powerful cultures on – in the history of the planet – one of them. I know how it’s been abused and everything else. Even personally, I know how some quarters have taken the range of my success, and lack of success in some of this – is something that makes me angry sometimes. Herbie and I talk about it. Herbie feels the same way, that people can’t be more open minded and not box you in. Because there ain’t no box for me. You think I’m proud of – you think I’m ashamed of Thriller? You know, not a chance. Not a chance. Because I could do the other thing too. If you can do all of it, you should do it.
If you can’t do it, shut up.
Don’t sit there and tell me about what Stanley Crouch thinks. I don’t care. Are you kidding?
I love Wynton, but please, don’t tell me what to do musically. You do what you do, and I’ll do what I do.
I’m hoping those pernicious influences are diminishing. I don’t think it’s . . .
I hope so, too, because it’s narrow-minded.
